title: 微观经济学导论：课程介绍与经济学模型
titleEn: Introduction to Microeconomics: Course Overview and Economic Models

sections.heading: 课程背景与MIT的学术传统
sections.headingEn: Course Background and MIT's Academic Legacy

items.text: 现代经济学诞生于MIT，因为MIT引入了约束优化（constrained optimization）这套工具；世界（经济学的发展）正是在这里被推动的。
items.textEn: Modern economics was born at MIT because MIT introduced the tools of constrained optimization — 'the world was developed right here at MIT.'

items.text: 老师会在黑板/课件上写出每节课的内容大纲（outline），本讲覆盖：课程细节、什么是微观经济学、经济学如何使用模型（以供求模型为例）、以及如何通过模型教授权衡取舍（tradeoffs）。
items.textEn: The instructor outlines each lecture's coverage: course details, what micro is, how economics uses models (the supply model), and how models teach tradeoffs.

sections.heading: 经济学研究方法：简化模型

items.text: 经济学的研究方法是通过构建简化模型（simplified models）来教授权衡取舍。
items.textEn: Economics teaches tradeoffs by building simplified models.

items.text: 模型的技术定义：对两个或多个变量之间任何关系的描述，就是一个模型。
items.textEn: A model is technically 'the description of any relationship between two or more variables.'

items.text: 与物理学（如能量与质量的关系）不同，经济学没有科学定律和常数（scientific laws and constants）；经济学不是真正的自然科学，而是社会科学（social science）。
items.textEn: Unlike physics (energy–mass relationship), economics has no scientific laws and constants; it is a social science, not a 'real' science.

items.text: 因为我们没有放之四海皆准的刚性定律，必须用模型尽可能解释世界。
items.textEn: Without rigid, universally applicable laws, economists use models to explain the world as much as possible.

items.text: 构建模型必须在两个目标之间权衡：一是尽可能多地解释现象（explain as much as we can），二是模型要简约（parsimonious）以便教学和解出。
items.textEn: Modeling involves trading off two goals: explaining as much as possible vs. keeping models parsimonious so they can be taught and solved.

items.text: 模型越复杂越难教、越难解；因此需要一组简化假设（simplifying assumptions）。
items.textEn: The more complicated a model, the harder it is to teach and solve — hence a set of simplifying assumptions.

sections.heading: 简化假设：两种商品模型及其合理性

items.text: 面对提问'你真的只在两种商品之间权衡吗'：现实中你当然从来不只是在两种商品之间取舍，但我们会把模型写成你只有两种商品可选。
items.textEn: Re: 'Are you really just trading off two goods?' — of course not in reality, but we write models as if you are.

items.text: 用两种商品写成的模型能给你理解三、四种商品模型所需的全部直觉，只是数学更简单。
items.textEn: A two-goods model gives you all the intuition needed for models with three or four goods, just with easier math.

items.text: 关键结论：在两种商品模型中学到的一切，告诉你理解n种商品模型所需的全部知识，只是数学更容易——这是相当'无害'（non-offensive）的简化假设，因为它实际上不改变任何结论。
items.textEn: Everything learned in a two-goods model applies to an n-goods model, with easier math — a fairly 'non-offensive' simplifying assumption because it doesn't really change anything.

items.text: 我们也会做出一些'有毒且冒犯'（noxious and offensive）的简化假设；如果对它们感到不满、想探究去掉这些假设会发生什么，这正是你应该成为经济学专业学生（economics major）的原因——后续课程会把模型加回丰富性（add richness）再看结果。
items.textEn: We'll also make 'noxious and offensive' assumptions; being bothered by them and wanting to see what happens without them is exactly why you should be an economics major — later classes add richness to the models.

items.text: 统计学家George Box曾写道：'所有模型都是错的，但有些是有用的'（All models are wrong, but some are useful.）——这正是本课程建模方法的核心理念。
items.textEn: Statistician George Box wrote: 'All models are wrong, but some are useful' — the guiding philosophy for modeling in this course.

sections.heading: 三层教学法：数学、图形与直觉
sections.headingEn: Three-Level Teaching: Mathematical, Graphical, and Intuitive

items.text: 老师将从三个层面教授经济学：第一层是数学（mathematical）——MIT的方式；第二层是图形（graphical）；第三层是直觉（intuitive）。
items.textEn: Economics will be taught on three levels: mathematical (the MIT way), graphical, and intuitive.

items.text: 要想在这门课中成功，三个层面都需要理解；并非每个模型都会用到全部三种方式，但掌握三者才能真正理解所学内容。
items.textEn: To succeed in this class, you need to understand all three levels; not every model uses all three, but all three are needed to truly understand the material.

sections.heading: 第一个经济学模型：供求模型与亚当·斯密
sections.headingEn: The First Economic Model: Supply and Demand and Adam Smith

items.text: 课程从供求模型（model of supply and demand）开始——这是第一个经济学模型，由亚当·斯密（Adam Smith）于1776年在其奠基性著作《国富论》（The Wealth of Nations）中提出。
items.textEn: We start with the model of supply and demand — the very first economic model, developed by Adam Smith in 1776 in 'The Wealth of Nations,' the founding book of economics.

items.text: 亚当·斯密的问题：思考水和钻石两种商品——对生命而言，没有什么比水更必需，人离开水无法生存；没有什么比钻石更不必需（在当时钻石没有工业用途，只是小饰品 baubles）。
items.textEn: Adam Smith's question: compare water and diamonds — nothing is more essential to life than water; nothing less essential than diamonds (then mere baubles with no industrial uses).

items.text: 悖论（paradox）：水对生命必不可少，钻石无关紧要，然而钻石价格很高，水却几乎免费。'这怎么可能？'（How could this be?）
items.textEn: The paradox: water is essential, diamonds are not, yet diamonds are very expensive and water is essentially free — 'How could this be?'

items.text: 斯密的解答要点一：上述描述只是价格模型的一半——即需求（demand）侧；水的需求远远大于钻石的需求。
items.textEn: Part of Smith's answer: what was just described is only half the model — the demand side; the demand for water is much larger than the demand for diamonds.

items.text: 斯密的解答要点二：还没讨论的是供给（supply）侧——相对于钻石，水的供给更加庞大：水无处不在，钻石却稀有难寻。
items.textEn: The missing half is supply: the supply of water is even larger relative to diamonds — water is everywhere, diamonds are rare to find.

items.text: 斯密的结论：虽然钻石的需求不如水的需求大，但钻石的供给比水的供给小得多得多——价格由供给与需求双方共同决定。
items.textEn: Smith's conclusion: while the demand for diamonds is not as high as for water, the supply of diamonds is much, much smaller than that of water — price is determined by both supply and demand.
